description.narrative: The initiative ‘Promoting green livelihoods for women, especially women with disabilities, through the development of recycled handicraft product value chains in Hue City’ was proposed to simultaneously address two major challenges: gender inequality in access tolivelihoods and the need to transition to a circular economy – green economy model. In the context of the Vietnamese Government promoting a green growth strategy and waste reduction, supporting women – particularly women with disabilities – to participate in the recycled product value chain is both practical and sustainable. The project aims to support the formation of 3–5 women-led green livelihood groups, strengthen two women with disabilities clubs, and establish a cooperative model to create a solid organisational foundation for production and business. Through training courses in business management, recycled handicraft production techniques, andthe application of digital technology and AI in sales, the project will help at least 120 women improve their skills and at least 27 women find new jobs. Simultaneously, the project promotes market connectivity, builds brand identity, establishes sales points, operates e-commerce channels, and implements community outreach activities on environmental protection. By linking women, businesses and cooperatives in the recycled handicraft product value chain, the initiative not only generates sustainable income for women but also contributes to building Hue into a green, environmentally friendly tourist city. This is a model that can be replicated and is in line with the sponsor's priorities of empowering women economically and promoting a green economy.

participating-org.narrative: Established in 2015, Centre for Highland Natural Resource Governance Research (CEGORN) is a Science and Technology organization under the Vietnam Union of Science and Technology Associations (VUSTA). CEGORN has its operation focus on matters related to policy andlaw, involving activities to raise people’s awareness. It embraces great respect and appreciation towards indigenous knowledge, presented by its efforts and investment in analysis and integration of indigenous culture into actions to promote sustainable development. In addition to great hands-on experience in working with people of ethnic minorities, CEGORN staff are all well equipped with thorough understanding about women's rights, thereby, encourage them to raise their voices and contribute to promote gender equality. In terms of project management, CEGORN has its capacity to harness resources, which contributes to enhance the effectiveness of the project implementation.
